h1: Asawann Hotel Nong Khai — a central city hotel that works for its mall-side location and easy price
intro: If you come to Nong Khai without a car and want a place where you can step out straight into restaurants, a 7-Eleven and a shopping complex, Asawann Hotel is one of the cheapest central options reviewers keep recommending. body.html: Asawann Hotel is a 3-star city hotel on Mitraphap Road, in the Pho Chai sub-district of Mueang Nong Khai. Its clearest selling point is the location — the hotel is attached to the Asawann shopping complex, a few steps from restaurants, a 7-Eleven and shops in town. Many people choose it precisely because it's central: you can walk to eat and shop without a car, and there's free parking for those who drive in.

Room types run from Superior Twin and Superior Double up to a Suite for those who want more space. Rooms are simply done in white-and-green tones, with air conditioning, a fridge and free Wi-Fi. Most reviewers say the rooms are spacious and clean for the price, but to be fair, the hotel has been open for around a decade — room quality is inconsistent, and some older units could do with a refresh. A few reviews note that soundproofing between rooms isn't great, curtains can be thin enough to let in the morning light, and mattresses in some rooms are starting to sag. A renovated room is noticeably more comfortable.
"The staff were lovely — polite and friendly. Lots of choice at breakfast, the room was spacious and clean, and everything in town was an easy walk. Genuinely good value for what we paid."

What reviewers praise most consistently is the polite, friendly staff and good service — many say it's the reason they come back. Another frequent compliment is the varied, good-value breakfast. The hotel has an on-site restaurant, a banquet room, massage service and a 24-hour front desk. Because it's attached to the Asawann shopping complex, food and essentials are very easy to find without going far.

Be clear about the location. Asawann sits in central Nong Khai on the Mitraphap Road side, strong on in-town convenience rather than river views. The hotel itself isn't on the Mekong or by Tha Sadet Market — those are about a 10-minute drive away. If you plan to sit by the river or wander the market every evening, you'll need a ride. But if you want a base where restaurants and a convenience store are right outside the door, this location works better than a riverside stay set away from the shops.

Honestly, Asawann Hotel suits people who want a cheap, central base, valuing location and convenience over newness or design. A score of 9.1 from 161 Trip.com reviews shows most guests are happy with the price and service, while a TripAdvisor rating of 3.4, ranked around #9 of 18 Nong Khai hotels, reflects the inconsistent room quality. If you can accept that it's an ageing property with some tired rooms, it's a solid value pick in the heart of town.

A tip from reading the reviews: ask for a renovated or higher-floor room when you book or check in, because room quality varies and the newer ones are clearly more comfortable. If you're a light sleeper, pack an eye mask, as some curtains are thin. And because it's attached to the mall, it's an easy base to eat and shop in town before driving out to the river or crossing into Vientiane.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Asawann Hotel Nong Khai

faq.q: Where is Asawann Hotel Nong Khai and how do you get there?
faq.a: It's on Mitraphap Road, Pho Chai sub-district, Mueang Nong Khai, in the city centre and attached to the Asawann shopping complex. It's a few steps from a 7-Eleven, restaurants and town shops, and about a 10-minute drive from Tha Sadet Market and the Mekong riverfront. The railway station and the Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge are each around a 10-minute drive away, and there's free parking for self-drivers.

faq.q: How much does Asawann Hotel cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around THB 900/night for a Superior Double. A Superior Twin runs about THB 990, a Suite around THB 1,200 and a VIP Suite around THB 1,500. All rooms have air-con, a fridge and free Wi-Fi; prices vary by date and package, so always compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: What are the rooms like at Asawann Hotel, and who is it best for?
faq.a: Rooms are simply done in white-and-green tones, spacious and clean for the price, but quality is inconsistent and some are older. It's best for people who want a cheap, central base, valuing location and the convenience of walking to eat and shop over newness or river views. Ask for a renovated room when you book.

faq.q: Does Asawann Hotel have a swimming pool and breakfast?
faq.a: There's no swimming pool. But there is an on-site restaurant, a banquet room, massage service, a 24-hour front desk, and breakfast included in many packages. The breakfast has plenty of choice and most guests find it filling and good value.

faq.q: Is Asawann Hotel on the Mekong riverfront?
faq.a: No, it's not on the river. The hotel is in the city centre on the Mitraphap Road side, stronger on in-town convenience and its mall-side location than on river views. To reach the riverfront or Tha Sadet Market, it's about a 10-minute drive. If staying right on the water matters to you, look at a riverside stay in this same series.

faq.q: What do reviewers praise most about Asawann Hotel?
faq.a: Reviewers most consistently praise the polite, friendly staff and good service and the varied, good-value breakfast. Combined with a central location attached to the Asawann shopping complex — with a 7-Eleven and restaurants right outside — it earns a score of 9.1 from 161 Trip.com reviews.
